Outdoor Housing Enclosure (aka "Mew") for temporary housing of birds of prey during recovery from injury or otherwise preparing to be released back into the wild. This will be for our home-based non-profit, Loudoun Valley Raptor Center (https://www.loudounvalleyraptors.org). The Mew will be constructed using standard framing construction techniques, using pressure treated lumber. Windows of the mew will be constructed using ½” EMT conduit, spaced ½” apart between each bar and between the end bars and side walls. There can be ¼” tolerance in that (meaning it doesn't need to be precisely ½” between each one, but pretty close to it.) This is to prevent a predator from reaching in. ½” hardware cloth will be used as a predator deterrent and to protect humans and wildlife around the mew from the raptors. This will be used on the ground beneath the mew as well as on any exposed area of the mew (including walls, windows, and roof). Additionally, heavy-duty screen will be used on all exposed areas as well, to mitigate external parasites. Pea gravel will be used as a floor of the mew, to provide a safe and comfortable ground covering for the raptors, and to provide an easily cleanable surface that can be removed and replenished easily as needed. 4'x8' PVC or Coroplast will be used on the inside of the mew on solid surfaces to facilitate easy cleaning. The Mew will be constructed using standard framing techniques, with studs 16” on center. Windows and doors will be framed as per standard construction techniques. All walls will have horizontal support members every 24” The north or north-west facing wall (20' long), plus 4' of the side walls adjacent to this wall, will be sheathed & solid on the outside, to provide respite and protection from wind & weather. These walls will have 4x8 PVC sheet finishing on the interior of the mew. The remaining walls will have 2' of solid “knee wall” at the bottom, and a combination of screen (heavy duty) and hardware cloth for the remaining area of the walls on the outside of the mew. These walls will be covered in 1x4 slats, spaced ¾” apart on the interior of the mew. Topsoil & grass under the platform will be removed, providing a dirt base. A layer of ½” hardware cloth will be applied on the ground under the platform to protect from digging predators; this would extend 12” beyond the platform on all sides. The roof will be a 3:12 shed-roof (mono-slope) style, with 2/3 of the roof surface, closest to the solid walls, covered using metal roofing. The remaining 1/3 surface will be exposed, but protected using hardware cloth and heavy duty screen. The walls of the mew will be 10' high, with the angled roof extending above that. The interior height of the mew will be 10' high consistently, to accommodate hinged center wall. The interior of the mew, once construction is completed, would be covered in 6-8” of pea gravel. At both ends of the mew, there shall be a double-entry door system to prevent escape of the raptor. This will have a solid floor, a covered roof, and exposed walls (meaning hardware cloth and screen). The mew will have a two-piece opposing-hinged wall (i.e., essentially two wall sections, hinged on opposite sides of the mew, and with sliding bolts in the center to attach the sections to each other when in place) dividing the mew in two equal sections. These sections can be folded back against the walls to utilize the mew as a single, larger mew. This will allow the mew to function as either a single 12x20 mew, or as two 12x10 mews. The structure will be built on a 6x6 wood perimeter foundation, with ground beneath the 6x6's being excavated as needed to achieve level.

Shredded materials will be sent off-site for further processing or brokering. This accessory use is customarily incidental and subordinate to the primary operations and does not constitute a "junk yard" per zoning definitions. The proposed project consists of constructing a covered exterior deck measuring 28 feet by 15 feet (420 square feet total area). The deck will be attached to the primary structure and designed in accordance with the International Residential Code (IRC 2018/2021, as adopted by the jurisdiction) and all applicable local amendments. Structural Components: Footings: Cast-in-place reinforced concrete footings sized per soil conditions and frost depth requirements (minimum 12 in. diameter or as engineered). Footings will extend below the local frost line and bear on undisturbed native soil. Perimeter Foundation: A continuous concrete perimeter wall will be provided to enclose a crawl space beneath the deck, with adequate ventilation openings as required by IRC R408. Gravel fill will be placed within the perimeter to promote drainage and moisture control. Columns/Posts: Vertical supports will consist of 8-inch diameter concrete or engineered columns, anchored to the footings and designed to carry roof and deck loads. Anchors and post bases will comply with IRC R407 and R507. Framing: Floor framing to consist of pressure-treated lumber (minimum No. 2 grade Southern Pine or equivalent), sized and spaced in accordance with IRC Table R507.5. All framing members in contact with concrete will be pressure-treated or provided with an approved moisture barrier. Decking Surface: Decking boards will be preservative-treated or naturally durable lumber, installed with corrosion-resistant fasteners in accordance with IRC R317 and R507.2.3. Roof Structure: A covered roof will be supported by the deck framing and structural columns. Roof framing will be sized and installed per IRC Chapter 8 (Roof-Ceiling Construction), with appropriate load design for snow, wind, and dead loads. Connections & Hardware: All structural connections will utilize corrosion-resistant metal connectors (hot-dipped galvanized or stainless steel) rated for exterior use, in accordance with IRC R317.3 and R507.2.
